title: Jacob's disguise (Genesis 27)
hookLine: goat skins on his arms, Jacob steals his blind father's blessing
last: NOT FOR A BOWL OF STEW.

lines: AN OLD MAN WHO CAN'T SEE.
A BLESSING CAN'T BE TAKEN BACK.
cards: Isaac is old, and his eyes are so dim he can't see. He calls in Esau, his favorite: take your bow, hunt me some game, cook it the way I love it, and I'll bless you before I die.
In this story, a father's blessing, once spoken, can't be taken back. Rebekah is listening at the tent. She loves Jacob.
The moment Esau leaves for the field, she calls her younger son: bring me two young goats. We're going to make your father's favorite meal. And you're going to wear it.

teach.h: WILL IT WORK? NOT IS IT WRONG.
teach.b: Jacob's worry isn't whether it's wrong. It's whether it'll work. My brother is hairy, he says, and I'm smooth.
So Rebekah dresses him in Esau's best clothes, so he'll smell of the field, and ties goat skins on his hands and the smooth of his neck. Jacob walks in with the meal. Who are you, my son?
And Jacob lies: I am Esau thy firstborn. Isaac is suspicious. How did you find it so quickly?
Jacob even brings God into it: "Because the LORD thy God brought it to me."
Isaac says, come near, let me feel you, runs his hands over the goat skins, and says, in the King James Bible: "The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau." He hears it.
But the hands win, and the smell of the field, and he gives the blessing.
Then Esau walks in with the real meal, Isaac trembles, and Esau cries a great and bitter cry: "Bless me, even me also, O my father." Is not he rightly named Jacob?
Ya'akov sounds like heel, and like a word for one who grabs, who supplants. He's done it twice now.
The text never praises the trick, and it shows the cost: Jacob has to run for his life, and Rebekah never sees her favorite son again in the story.
Some readers, Jewish and Christian, see the promise going on through this grasping, frightened man. Not because of the lie, they say. In spite of it.

how: Many Christians practice regular confession, privately, with a pastor, or in the sacrament of reconciliation, naming specific wrongs, and Jacob's story is often preached as a sign that God works through flawed people without approving their wrongs.

s: Jacob refuses at first because it's wrong
his worry is whether it will work: his brother is hairy, and he is smooth.
Isaac notices the voice is Jacob's

games.q: you're Isaac, blind. the son in front of you sounds like Jacob but feels hairy like Esau and smells of the field. what do you do?
o: send him away until you're sure.
trust the hands and give the blessing.
games.why: "the voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau," and the hands win. the blessing can't be taken back.

practice: Goat skins come in modern sizes: a little lie to get out of something, a version of yourself you put on for a boss, a parent, a date, a favor you took that was meant for someone else.

Let one small one come to mind, and without excusing it or drowning in it, name it honestly to yourself: that voice was mine. If you pray, you can bring it to God, and ask whether there's one thing to set right.
